The data form includes fields like number of randomized patients, surgery type, ASA distribution, total fluid administered, types of fluids (crystalloids and colloids), blood loss, morbidity events, mortality, hospital LOS, and others.

Looking at the "n_randomized_gdft" and "n_randomized_control", I'll check the Results section. The article mentions 42 patients in the SOC group and 43 in the GDFT group, so these are the numbers to use. 

For "surgery_type", the Methods section lists the types of surgeries, which are all open abdominal procedures. I'll note that as a single entry since all surgeries fall under the same category.

Next, "laparoscopy_gdft" and "laparoscopy_control" should be "0" because all surgeries were open, not laparoscopic.

The ASA distribution is given in Table 1. Both groups have similar distributions, so I'll list them as SOC: 11 I, 26 II, 5 III and GDFT: 7 I, 28 II, 5 III.

For total fluid, crystalloids, and colloids, Table 2 provides the data. GDFT group had a lower total fluid, mainly due to less crystalloids, while colloids were similar. Blood loss is also provided in the same table.

Morbidity events are discussed in the Results under postoperative complications. SOC had 19 patients (45%) with PPC, and GDFT had 6 (14%). Mortality was 4 in SOC and 2 in GDFT, but not statistically significant.

Hospital LOS is mentioned in the Results as median days, so I'll use the provided values. Other fields like inotrope_use, time_to_flatus, etc., are either not reported or zero as per the article.

I need to make sure I'm using the correct sections as per the "where" field. Each value is transcribed exactly as reported, keeping the units and decimal places as in the article. If a datum isn't present, I'll mark it as "NR".

Finally, I'll structure all this information into the JSON format, ensuring each field is correctly labeled and sourced from the appropriate section of the article.
